paper_style.palette_strategy: Tables use black text and black booktabs rules. Figure 1 combines grayscale input, a blue-gray-red diverging signed map, and a magma sequential map; Figures 2 and 3 use blue/red method hues with additional light/dark variation, with no complete key for the second channel.
paper_style.vector_raster_mix: The PDF embeds raster image panels and colorbars for Figure 1 while its labels/contours are vector; Figures 2 and 3 are vector bars/text; all tables are vector text/rules.
paper_style.style_consistency: Serif typography, restrained annotation, single-column charts, double-column Figure 1, and booktabs tables are consistent across the paper. Caption completeness and color-key coverage are inconsistent: Figure 1 is explanatory, while most other captions are title-only.

figures.label: Figure 1

caption.text: Figure 1. ANOVA-Based Shapley Values on the Binarized MNIST Dataset. We apply our framework on a MLP trained on binarized MNIST, encoded as a tabular dataset of shape (60 000, 784). The attribution targets the predicted probability of the specific class ‘3’, defined as f(x) := P(MLP(x) = 3). (Left) The original input sample (digit ‘8’). (Middle) Signed local attributions: red pixels increase the probability of the target class ‘3’, while blue pixels decrease it. (Right) Absolute attribution magnitudes. We observe a behavior consistent with the nature of the digits. The pixels on the right side, which overlap with the shape of a ‘3’, positively contribute to the target probability (red). Conversely, the pixels on the left side close the loops, acting as the distinguishing features between an ‘8’ and a ‘3’; these pixels correctly penalize the target probability (blue), allowing the model to rule out class ‘3’.

color.semantic_mapping: Left panel uses grayscale input; middle panel maps negative/zero/positive attribution to blue/gray/red; right panel maps absolute magnitude with magma; black and white contours outline the input digit.

encodings.y: 28×28 pixel row/position within each image panel
encodings.color: input grayscale; signed attribution sign and magnitude; absolute attribution magnitude
encodings.line: black contour in signed panel and white contour in absolute panel

figures.data_and_statistics: One binarized MNIST sample of 28×28 pixels (source cell sample index 44162) is attributed to class 3 via f(x)=P(MLP(x)=3); the caption reports the tabular dataset shape (60 000, 784). No repeats, intervals, error bars, or uncertainty encoding are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Results headline and method-interface qualitative evidence: the three views connect the ANOVA-Shapley output to a local prediction, with right-side pixels increasing class-3 probability and loop-closing left pixels decreasing it; Table 7 later quantifies the MNIST rank-budget/reconstruction setting.
design_strengths: Three panels preserve the same pixel geometry and give a short input→signed contribution→magnitude reading path.
Separate diverging and sequential colorbars make sign versus magnitude explicit.
Digit contours and the long caption connect visual regions to the class-3 versus class-8 mechanism.
design_weaknesses: Colorbars provide only qualitative endpoints and no attribution units or probability change.
There is no sample identifier, predicted probability, repeat, or uncertainty display.
Bilinear interpolation smooths discrete pixels; signed red/blue semantics are not grayscale-safe.
figures.reusable_pattern: For local explanations, use aligned input, signed-attribution, and absolute-attribution panels with separate explicit colorbars, and bind sign, target class, and sample context in the caption.

caption.text: Figure 2. Global Feature Importance on MUSHROOMS dataset.

color.semantic_mapping: Blue hue identifies ANOVA and red hue identifies TreeSHAP; within each hue, unkeyed lightness differences appear across bars, while bar length and printed values encode relative ℓ1 norm.

figures.data_and_statistics: Global main-effect and TreeSHAP importance is shown as relative ℓ1 norm in percent for ten features. ANOVA values are 29.36, 22.91, 18.91, 6.66, 6.32, 4.65, 4.19, 3.16, 2.88, 0.48; TreeSHAP values are 24.17, 18.45, 17.16, 9.70, 3.83, 6.23, 0.74, 0.31, 0.15, 0.84. The p.7 prose identifies odor/X5, gill color/X9, and spore print color/X20 as the leading features in 8,124 observations and 22 variables. No repeats or uncertainty are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Main-comparison/mechanism evidence: exact ANOVA main effects are placed against TreeSHAP to compare global feature ranking and expose the leading MUSHROOMS features.
design_strengths: A common linear scale and direct numeric labels make method differences visible for each feature.
The horizontal orientation accommodates feature labels and preserves a shared ranking.
Hue, bar length, and values provide several cues for the method comparison.
design_weaknesses: The caption is title-only and omits the ℓ1 normalization, feature selection, data scope, and aggregation setting.
Within-series lightness has no legend meaning, and the blue/red method encoding is not grayscale-safe.
Small single-column labels and the absence of uncertainty or repeat information limit auditability.
figures.reusable_pattern: For global importance comparisons, retain one feature order and one x scale, use two clearly keyed method hues with direct values, and define normalization, data scope, and every color channel in the caption.

figures.data_and_statistics: Twenty global-importance bars compare ANOVA and attention rollout. ANOVA suit values are approximately 2.3, 1.8, 1.6, 1.6, 1.6 and rank values 18.2, 18.3, 18.1, 18.2, 18.3; Attention Roll suit values are 6.9 for each position and rank values 13.1 for each position. The surrounding p.8 prose sets r_low := 5,000 for the rank approximation and aggregates local Shapley values in ℓ1 norm; no uncertainty or repeats are shown.
figures.evidence_relation: Main-comparison/mechanism evidence for the high-dimensional sparse POKER HAND experiment: it compares the closed-form ANOVA importance with attention rollout and exposes a rank-versus-suit structure.
design_strengths: The fixed card-position order preserves the data's suit/rank structure instead of collapsing it into one aggregate.
A common y scale and direct values make the repeated rank/suit pattern easy to inspect.
Blue/red hue separates methods while light/dark shades provide a second structural cue.
design_weaknesses: The suit/rank lightness channel has no independent key and can be confused with method color.
The title-only caption omits the rank budget, aggregation definition, and attention-rollout setup.
Small labels, no uncertainty, and visually uneven-looking tick intervals reduce single-column readability.
figures.reusable_pattern: When features have a fixed position×type structure, use grouped bars in the native order and reserve separate, explicitly keyed channels for method and feature type.

tables.label: Table 6

caption.text: Table 6. Performance & Metrics. Top: Fast approximation restricted to main effects (r_main). Bottom: Higher rank approximation (r_low) for reconstruction analysis.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, interval, repeat, or error-bar encoding is present in the PDF table.
tables.data_and_statistics: Two three-row panels report DATASET, rank budget (r_main in the top panel and r_high in the bottom header), Time, R², MSE, and Rel. MSE. Top: Poker Hand=(76,1.8s,.003,.24,49%); Connect-4=(83,10s,.45,.07,13%); Dota2=(112,23s,.36,.02,6%). Bottom: Poker=(5,000,10min,.79,.05,10%); Connect-4=(5,000,37min,.70,.04,7%); Dota2=(4,000,39min,.41,.01,5%). The PDF caption says r_low for the bottom panel while the table header and prose say r_high; both strings are retained as observed.
tables.evidence_relation: p.8 links the main-effects fast approximation to the higher-rank reconstruction setting and makes the runtime–accuracy boundary visible for the three sparse datasets.
design_strengths: Top/bottom row groups separate the cheap main-effects regime from higher-rank reconstruction.
Time, explained-variance-style score, MSE, and relative MSE are aligned in one compact comparison.
design_weaknesses: The caption/table do not define R², MSE, relative-MSE denominator, hardware, or repeat count.
The caption's r_low versus header/prose r_high inconsistency is a reproducibility defect.
Six columns and two repeated headers are dense in a single column.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use explicitly labeled budget groups to show the cost frontier, but define each metric, unit, environment, and naming convention at the table boundary.

tables.label: Table 8

caption.text: Table 8. Comparison between our closed-form ANOVA and TreeHFD.

tables.uncertainty: No uncertainty, interval, repeat, or error-bar encoding is present in the PDF table.
tables.evidence_relation: Appendix C p.17–p.18 compares closed-form ANOVA with TreeHFD in the synthetic full-support, even-d setting; XGBoost uses 100 trees and max depth 2, and the two grouped metric families quantify orthogonality and indicator differences.
design_strengths: The two-level header separates orthogonality from method-indicator discrepancies.
Scientific notation retains the very small errors without visual saturation.
Minimal rules and no vertical grid preserve the paper's table language.
design_weaknesses: The caption omits the XGBoost training details, synthetic function, and exact discrepancy definitions.
The table requires Appendix C prose to interpret Closed-Form, TreeHFD, and the two difference columns.
tables.reusable_pattern: Use a grouped multi-level header when two metric families answer distinct validation questions, and keep tiny errors in scientific notation with definitions adjacent to the table.

cross_object_system.visual_narrative: The objects progress from Figure 1's local explanation interface and Table 1's analytic sanity check through Tables 2–4's low-dimensional agreement tests, Figures 2–3's global importance comparisons, Tables 5–7's sparse-scale budget/reconstruction trade-offs, and Appendix Table 8's TreeHFD baseline.
cross_object_system.caption_system: Figure 1 is the only self-contained explanatory caption; Figures 2–3 and most tables are title-only. Table 6 adds a setup sentence, while Tables 3–4 expose only the ISE label and scaling in the title. Definitions, units, denominators, repeats, and model settings mostly remain in prose.
cross_object_system.table_header_system: Booktabs rules, serif type, no vertical lines, and compact one-level headers dominate. Table 6 uses repeated panel headers and Table 8 uses a two-level grouped header; these are the clearest structural devices in the table system.
cross_object_system.method_result_ablation_link: Figure 1 and Tables 1–4 connect the closed-form ANOVA mechanism to local and low-dimensional agreement; Figures 2–3 extend it to global feature importance; Tables 5–7 expose sparse-scale rank and runtime costs; Table 8 provides an appendix baseline comparison.
cross_object_system.main_appendix_link: Main-text Figure 1/Table 7 and Figures 2–3/Tables 5–6 establish local, global, and efficiency evidence; Appendix C Table 8 tests the formulation against TreeHFD under its full-support synthetic assumptions, with interpretation continuing on p.18.
cross_object_system.typography_consistency: Figures and tables use a stable Times New Roman/Nimbus Roman/Computer Modern serif family. Tables remain near 10 pt; chart titles are near 10 pt and chart legends/annotations are reduced to roughly 4–8 pt, creating a predictable but sometimes dense single-column hierarchy.
cross_object_system.color_consistency: Tables are monochrome and grayscale-safe. Figures share blue/red comparison hues or explicit diverging/sequential maps, but Figures 2–3 add undocumented lightness channels and none of the chart palettes is fully grayscale-safe; Figure 1 has the strongest semantic redundancy through panel position and contour.

most_reusable_patterns: Aligned input/signed/absolute attribution panels with separate signed and magnitude colorbars.
Budget-grouped tables that put rank, runtime, and reconstruction metrics on one comparison surface.
Two-level metric headers and scientific notation for distinct validation families with tiny discrepancies.
highest_value_objects: Figure 1 is the strongest explanatory object because it binds method output, visual encoding, target class, and a concrete mechanism in one caption.
Table 6 most directly exposes the practical cost frontier between main-effects and higher-rank reconstruction.
Table 8 is the clearest appendix validation layout because its grouped header separates orthogonality from indicator agreement.
failure_patterns: Title-only captions leave estimands, denominators, units, aggregation, repeats, and model settings outside the object boundary.
Figures 2–3 use a second color/lightness channel without a complete key and are not grayscale-safe.
Single-column charts use small labels and no uncertainty/repeat display; Table 6 also contains an r_low/r_high naming inconsistency.
Public author sources do not include exact Figure 2/3 or table-generation files, limiting visual reproducibility.
final_judgment.one_sentence_visual_strategy: The paper uses a restrained serif/booktabs system to move from local ANOVA explanations to global comparisons and rank-cost trade-offs, and would become substantially more reusable by making every caption self-contained, keying every color channel, and publishing exact chart/table sources.
